value.name: Rosa recalls his childhood crying
value.description: Rosa recognizes and remembers seeing him cry only once before, when he was eleven and missed a team he wanted to make.
evidence: y of crying Rosa had seen him do once before, when he was eleven and had failed to make a team he had wanted to make, and which she had not seen him do since.

value.name: He blames her mother for being wrong
value.description: After crying, he says that she was wrong about what would be kind.
evidence: "She was wrong," he said, after a while. "She was wrong about what would be kind."

value.name: Rosa defends her mother’s view of him
value.description: Rosa says their mother was often wrong about him by thinking better of him than he thought of himself, and frames it as a challenge sons must meet or fail to recover from.
evidence: "She was wrong," Rosa said. "She was often wrong about you. She was wrong about you in the direction of thinking better of you than you thought of yourself, which is a direction mothers are often wrong in, and which it is the work of sons to either grow into or never recover from. I do not know yet which you are going to do. I am hopeful."

value.name: He laughs through tears
value.description: He responds to Rosa with a brief wet, startled laugh, showing emotional release.
evidence: He laughed, once, a wet startled laugh.

value.name: He refuses to sell the house
value.description: He tells Rosa plainly that he does not want to sell the house.
evidence: "I do not want to sell the house."

value.name: He admits uncertainty about the house
value.description: He says he does not know what to do with the house, but has known since Wednesday afternoon that he does not want to sell it.
evidence: "I do not know what I want to do with it. But I do not want to sell it. I have known I did not want to sell it since Wednesday afternoon when I sat in the dining room and I could not get the words out of my mouth,"

value.name: He stops rationalizing the sale
value.description: He explains that he has been trying to invent a story that would force him to sell the house, but he is exhausted by the effort and cannot sustain the justification.
evidence: "and I have been trying since then to find a story I could tell myself in which I had to sell it anyway because of the debts and the taxes and the practicality, and I have not been able to find one that holds together for more than an hour at a time, and I am tired of looking for one."

value.name: Rosa urges him to stop searching
value.description: Rosa tells him to stop looking for a justification and simply stop.

value.name: He raises debt concerns
value.description: He points out that debts still remain as a practical obstacle to keeping the house.

value.name: Rosa reassures him about the house
value.description: Rosa argues that debts are always present, but the house has endured for 140 years and can outlast his debts too.
evidence: "There are always debts. The house has been there for a hundred and forty years and it has outlasted every debt anyone in it ever had. It will outlast yours."

value.name: Rosa proposes financial alternatives
value.description: Rosa begins listing possible ways to keep the house, including second mortgages and equity arrangements.
evidence: "There are ways. There are second mortgages, and there are equity arrangements, and there"
